formula: I take your point, but + clause

formulas.formula: I take your point, but + clause

example: I take your point, but the cost cannot simply be ignored.
exampleZh: 我明白你的觀點，但我們不能完全不考慮成本。

examples.en: I take your point, but the cost cannot simply be ignored.
examples.zh: 我明白你的觀點，但我們不能完全不考慮成本。
examples.highlight: I take your point, but the cost cannot simply be ignored.

rules.zh: 後面需要完整子句有主語和動詞，因此是完整子句。
rules.en: But I take your point, but the cost is too high. I take your point, but the high cost. The cost is too high

rules.zh: 前面通常使用逗號在清晰、完整的書面英語中，兩個完整子句由 but 連接時，通常在 but 前加逗號。
rules.en: But I take your point**, but** we need more evidence. I take your point but we need more evidence.

rules.zh: 這個句型表示「部分認同」，不是完全同意我明白你的觀點，但這項建議仍有幾個弱點。 說話者承認對方的觀點有道理，但仍然提出不同看法。
rules.en: I take your point, but the proposal still has several weaknesses.

rules.zh: 後面應提出真正相關的保留我明白你對減價的看法，但公司仍然需要支付營運成本。 後半部分與討論無關。
rules.en: But Natural: I take your point about reducing the price, but the company still needs to cover its costs. Unnatural: I take your point about reducing the price, but my brother likes football.

rules.zh: 後面可以是陳述句或真正相關的問題我明白你的觀點，但證據並不完整。 我明白你的觀點，但額外資金從何而來？
rules.en: But Statement: I take your point, but the evidence is incomplete. Question: I take your point, but where would the extra money come from?

rules.zh: 本練習不使用其他相近表達代替核心句型以下說法意思相近，但不是本課的目標：【I see your point, but...；I understand your point, but...；You may be right, but...；I agree to some extent, but...；That is a fair point, but...】 所有答案必須包含：【I take your point】
rules.en: I see your point, but... I understand your point, but... You may be right, but... I agree to some extent, but... That is a fair point, but... I take your point

benefits.zh: 這個句型讓你先表示自己有聆聽和理解對方，然後才提出不同意見，語氣會比直接否定對方更有禮貌。你的想法行不通。 我明白你的觀點，但這個想法可能很難實行。 第二句仍然表達不同意，但聽起來較冷靜和尊重對方。
benefits.en: It helps you disagree politely Instead of rejecting another person’s idea immediately, you first show that you have listened to and understood it. Compare: Your idea will not work. I take your point, but the idea may be difficult to put into practice.

benefits.zh: 這個句型讓你先承認其中一方面有道理，再提出另一方面，使回應顯得更加全面和平衡。
benefits.en: It makes your response balanced The structure lets you recognise one side of an argument before introducing another side.

benefits.zh: 當對方知道你明白他的觀點時，他通常會更願意繼續聆聽你的回應。這對會議、課堂討論和小組工作特別有用。
benefits.en: It helps discussions continue calmly People are more likely to continue listening when they feel that their ideas have been understood.

benefits.zh: 這是一個實用的說話框架。你可以先說 I take your point, but...，再加入你的憂慮、問題或另一種看法，令即時回應更容易組織。
benefits.en: It gives you a ready-made speaking frame You do not need to plan the whole response from the beginning. You can begin with: I take your point, but... and then add your concern, question or alternative view.

benefits.zh: 在討論、簡報和工作訊息中，你有時需要承認某個建議有道理，同時解釋為甚麼它仍然不足。這個句型能清楚引入反方觀點或限制。
benefits.en: It helps you introduce counterarguments In discussions, presentations and professional messages, you often need to respond to a reasonable idea while explaining why it may not be sufficient.

benefits.zh: 你可以使用 about + 名詞／V-ing 或 that + 子句，清楚指出自己正在回應對方的哪一個觀點，避免意思含糊。
benefits.en: The optional extensions make your meaning more precise You can use about + noun / V-ing or that + clause to show exactly which point you are answering.
